scope: Systems/content audit only. No production changes. Browser, campaign soaks, broad tests, networking and art acceptance belong to sibling audits.

priorityDefinitions.P0: Stop immediately: demonstrated catastrophic integrity/security failure or generally unplayable campaign. None established by this audit.
priorityDefinitions.P1: Must resolve or explicitly renegotiate scope before premium 1.0; serious exploit or defining release-system gap.
priorityDefinitions.P2: Important depth/usability/presentation improvement after blocking foundations. Some still belong to declared release gates.

effortDefinitions.M: Bounded cross-package change with tests and save considerations
effortDefinitions.XXL: Multi-system content and implementation program; not a single ticket

findings.title: Legal stacks above twenty formations become unattackable
findings.impact: A player can deny field combat and settlement conquest by keeping at least twenty-one formations on a hex. This removes intended victory-project counterplay and can freeze fronts; army-container capacity does not constrain total co-located formations.
findings.current: Field attack sums all defenders and rejects above twenty. Siege assault does the same; direct field attacks on town garrisons are forbidden. Normal queue production creates singleton armies on their town without a stack-wide limit. Siege supplies only affect militia morale, not the twenty-one actual garrison formations.
findings.verification: probes.ts succeeded. A fresh generated world reached twenty-one co-located scouts on turn 52 using twenty paid recruitments, three paid buildings and real turns, no injected state. Separate save-valid authored field fixture rejected twenty-one and accepted twenty; authored garrison stayed at twenty-one / 1260 strength after ten siege turns and still rejected assault at zero defenses and supplies. Rejections did not mutate the state hash; saved continuations validated.
findings.recommendation: Define bounded battle participation plus reserves/reinforcement or an explicit legal strategic stacking policy. Never silently delete excess troops. Preserve a way to attack every reachable hostile stack and siege every reachable town; test 20, 21 and larger field/garrison/fleet stacks through paid production, save/load and AI.
dependencies: AI force assembly and target selection

findings.title: Prosperity is the only terminal victory path
findings.impact: All strategies converge on the same three-town economic project. Military conquest is an input to Prosperity, not an implemented Dominion victory, and elimination is not a separate ending.
findings.current: Victory schema literally permits only prosperity, set only when the Hearth Exchange completes. Gates require at least three distinct tested victories; MASTER_PROMPT asks for five named paths. Standard/Long/Epic mainly increase Civic accounts and project prices/response windows, not the strategic systems between them.
findings.verification: Imported victory schema and traced project eligibility, pause/cancellation, progress and end-turn guard. No complete campaign was run by this subagent.
findings.recommendation: Agree the release path set before content expansion. Implement genuinely distinct progress, public warnings, terminal predicates and recoverable counterplay for the agreed additional paths; verify at least three under Gate B without silently dropping the five-path product target. Add explicit defeat/elimination handling and earned long-game outcome evidence.
dependencies: Diplomatic and supernatural rules for paths that rely on them

findings.title: Twenty-four cultures do not yet provide twenty-four strategic rule identities
findings.impact: Faction selection changes ecological optimization, presentation and AI recruitment preference, but not access to units, casters, research, victory conditions or political obligations. Replay differences are much narrower than the lore promises.
findings.current: Twenty-four stable culture definitions, signed biome affinities and name pools are real. All recruit the same thirteen units at the same prices. All Waykeepers start Flame 1/Rune 1. Nineteen recruitment-weight vectors exist; the first six cultures share one. Extra campaign seats repeat definitions, not new cultures or ancestries.
findings.verification: Imported all definitions and deduplicated weight vectors; traced initial state, production prerequisites and caster recruitment.
findings.recommendation: Build a small contrast cohort of original faction mechanics, each with an economic constraint, military or magical exception and opponent counterplay, before expanding all cultures. Retain the shared engine; add data-driven capabilities rather than faction-specific engine forks. Treat count targets as unmet until distinct decisions or a documented non-filler equivalent are demonstrated.
dependencies: AI valuation of new capability data

findings.title: Magic is a correct two-spell battle foundation, not the promised strategic system
findings.impact: The core fantasy strategy differentiation is missing: map-changing magical competition, scarce caster access and supernatural counterplay cannot arise from two universal battle actions.
findings.current: Two Arcane Theory purchases, two personal paths, two spells (damage and ward), one fixed caster role. No exported rituals, summons, recipes/items/relics, sacred/occult progression or discoverable magical sites. Ashglass is an arcane-category resource, but its current material consumers are civic development, not spells or rituals.
findings.verification: Validated exported content, inspected complete canonical command/state shapes and traced actual national/personal checks plus resource-cost consumers. No browser casting claim.
findings.recommendation: First close one original map-level magical loop: site discovery, paid resource/caster eligibility, strategic effect, visible warning and counteraction, with AI/save/replay. Then extend schools, faction access, artifice and sacred/occult content in tested batches; do not inflate counts by treating research unlocks and their same spells as independent effects.

findings.title: Diplomacy stops at war and paid truces; political relationships are not executable
findings.impact: No alternate way to organize power, negotiate access, form coalitions or make a client network. Internal tensions authored in the lore have no political rule consequences.
findings.current: Only one-way coin peace terms plus 5-30 turn binding truces. Trust/respect are recorded but absent from peace utility and war selection. Grievances and war age do affect peace. No access, alliance, guarantee, tribute/client, settlement/resource exchange or intelligence clauses; four capture outcomes omit client rule. No ruler/loyalty/succession/rebellion state.
findings.verification: Traced complete diplomacy state and evaluator, AI diplomatic policy, capture enum and canonical state. Detached observations with trust -100/respect 0 and trust 100/respect 100 returned identical peace assessments in an executed probe.
findings.recommendation: Deliver a bounded clause/obligation foundation beginning with access, exchange and client/tribute relationships, including breach and AI valuation. Connect meaningful relationship memory to actual decisions. Add only strategically scoped internal pressure needed by the selected factions/path, not a life-simulation wishlist.

findings.title: The middle and late campaign have no independent actors, authored event choices or epochs
findings.impact: Exploration finds geography, resources and peer realms but no independent political ecology or authored discoveries. Once common development is exhausted, the remaining activity is expansion, repeated war and funding the same project.
findings.current: No exported minor-power, landmark, quest or branching-event registries, and no corresponding canonical actor/event/epoch state. Ruins are generated by razing existing towns, not authored dungeon/site content. Domain events are factual action logs; they are not 150 context-aware event templates. Turn resolution advances the existing economy, combat support and project systems only.
findings.verification: Imported all content exports, indexed the strict command/state boundary and inspected founding/raze and turn phase code. Absence is bounded to the audited production architecture; no claim that lore lacks these ideas.
findings.recommendation: Author one bounded independent-power/site/event loop with persistent consequences and AI choices, then a state-triggered epoch/crisis that changes priorities rather than just prices. Establish decision-density and counterplay evidence before targeting hundreds of turns. Expand templates only after the runtime loop works.

findings.title: Starvation and insolvency barely constrain an already-built empire
findings.impact: Food deficits only stop growth; depleted treasuries only subtract one movement (minimum one). Unpaid troops retain strength and recover morale/fatigue. Supply pressure cannot defeat a stranded field force or real garrison, weakening economic, siege and logistics counterplay.
findings.current: Food is clamped to zero with no starvation loss. Upkeep is clamped to zero debt, and the sole shortfall hook is movement -1. Morale +10 and fatigue -15 are unconditional for formations each turn. Siege supply depletion affects militia morale only.
findings.verification: An explicitly authored save-valid population-200 town with food yield 11 versus consumption 800 and zero treasury remained population 200 for ten real turns. One unpaid heavy formation stayed strength 85, recovered morale from 20 to 85/fatigue from 60 to 0, and kept movement 1. This proves rules behavior, not earned population-200 reachability or campaign exploit frequency.
findings.recommendation: Choose explicit, telegraphed famine/arrears/supply consequences with a recovery path and bounded implementation. Make siege isolation affect actual defending formations. Avoid adding punishing attrition without logistics UI and AI planning; test sustained deficits, recovery and no insolvency softlock.

findings.title: Functional AI is integrated but strategic personalities, theaters and difficulty are not
findings.impact: The engine can legally use many systems, but major rivals tend toward a common economic plan and local opportunistic war. Pacing choices cannot substitute for skilled, differentiated opposition over a long campaign.
findings.current: Observation-only planner coordinates budgets, research, land, officers, fleets, merging, target movement and victory-host safety. It adopts Charter compact specifically, chooses doctrine from current war/no-war, builds the first missing non-coastal building in shared order, and attacks adjacent unprotected forces when their observed strength fits. No persistent national-goal/theater/operation state or difficulty setting is present in the audited canonical/options/planner interfaces.
findings.verification: Code review, not an AI competency soak. Existing status documents a Standard/four-seat contact regression; this audit does not reclassify that historical report as a fresh test result.
findings.recommendation: Retain the legal proposal architecture. Add bounded, saved strategic commitments and theater coordination tied to distinct victory threats/faction capabilities; expose disclosed difficulty policy separately from pace. Validate multiple earned campaign trajectories and contact/overseas counterplay, not only one-turn command presence.

findings.title: Tactical deployment is fixed by creation IDs rather than player intent
findings.impact: Composition and positioning matter, yet the player cannot deliberately place the pike screen ahead of missiles or arrange a reserve. Identical role purchases can occupy different ranks based on unrelated serial allocation.
findings.current: Deployment sorts formation IDs lexicographically then assigns row=floor(index/5), column=index%5. Four army-wide orders exist. Individual soldiers are canonical casualties, not individually commanded tactical agents. Arbalester, pike and mounted rules have real effects.
findings.verification: Traced deployment and command schemas plus tactical kernel. No outcome comparison from renamed identities was run, so the claim concerns layout control, not a measured win-rate change.
findings.recommendation: Provide a compact deployment policy/formation-slot control with preview and a sensible role-aware default, plus matching AI placement. Keep the shared fast deterministic kernel; an RTS command layer is not necessary.

findings.title: Material economy has extraction but few strategic dependencies and no bilateral trade
findings.impact: Deposits create site decisions and progression costs, but denying horses does not prevent cavalry, denying iron does not prevent heavy recruitment, and luxury/arcane labels do not produce distinct happiness or casting systems. Late surpluses funnel into an unlimited fixed-price coin sink.
findings.current: Eight resources, eight extraction improvements, fourteen material-cost development nodes; sales consume own stock at an owned active market. Unit/building schemas have coin and industry costs but no material costs. No buy, bilateral resource exchange, route demand or processing-chain commands.
findings.verification: Imported registries and traced all production material-cost consumers; compared with production and sale implementations. No balance claim about dominant income sources without sibling campaign measurements.
findings.recommendation: Before multiplying resources to forty, connect a few to meaningful substitution, recruitment/equipment or ritual choices and one genuine exchange/access mechanism. Give every new resource a distinct contestable use; preserve affordability and catch-up options.

findings.title: Generated names and skill trees do not yet create political or narrative characters
findings.impact: Officers are valuable military attachments but culturally named replacements share the same role parameters. Lore biographies do not become campaign relationships, choices or notable people.
findings.current: Four roles, three missions, seventeen skill definitions, one Rally; twenty-four 8x8 name pools yield 1536 distinct unsuffixed names. Naming uses global serial and appends cycles. No authored biography-bearing characters, trait/loyalty/relationship/office systems; Waykeeper has no skill nodes and fixed aptitude.
findings.verification: Programmatic distinct-name count; role/skill imports; canonical character schema, recruitment and mission inspection. Names are a real procedural naming pool, not proof of 1536 unique biographies.
findings.recommendation: Attach a small set of original, state-triggered traits/relationships or office conflicts to actual mission and battle histories. Give caster differentiation real eligibility/cost effects. Do not expand names alone to claim notable-character depth.
dependencies: Lore canon and factual chronicle constraints

findings.title: Production queues cannot be cancelled or reprioritized through a public command
findings.impact: A player can commit up to five orders, but cannot undo a mistaken queue or switch priorities during an emerging war; conquest clears it, ordinary management does not.
findings.current: The only production command is queue; upfront coin payment, progress accumulation and FIFO completion are implemented. There is no cancel/reorder production command in the complete current discriminated command schema. Land work and travel have explicit cancellation, so the omission is specific to production.
findings.verification: Imported complete command schema and traced queue and completion code. Browser affordance audit remains with parent.
findings.recommendation: Define cancellation/reordering with explicit coin refund and sunk-industry policy, then add canonical commands and UI/AI consumers. Test partial construction, naval berth interruption, capture and save/replay so cancellation cannot mint value.

findings.title: No audio implementation or tracked audio assets found in bounded production scan
findings.impact: No evidenced music, ambience, command feedback or battle sound layer supports premium presentation. Visual animation alone cannot supply the missing audio feedback.
findings.current: Scanned 179 tracked non-test production TypeScript/TSX files for browser audio APIs, common audio libraries, audio extensions and audio/music/sfx/volume/mute terms: zero hits. All tracked repository filenames contain no matched audio extension.
findings.verification: Reproducible source/filename scan in inventory.ts; exact file set and regexes retained in audio-search.json. Not a browser listening or network-capture test; CSS/HTML, external streaming or untracked assets are outside the source scan.
findings.recommendation: Coordinate with art audit: specify a restrained original audio palette, user-gesture activation, separate music/effects volumes and mute, saved preferences and bounded voice counts. Trigger playback from confirmed presentation/domain facts, never from a second combat simulation; record licensing/provenance.

findings.title: Research design checkpoint predates the current resource/development expansion
findings.impact: A reader can mistake the slice-23 checkpoint's eleven skills and absent magical-resource economy language for a current content inventory, despite slice-27 having seventeen skills and an arcane-category deposit.
findings.current: The checkpoint is explicitly dated and aspirational sections are honestly labeled, so it is not a fraudulent completion claim. README and current status are newer and correctly state the two-spell and broader-release limitations.
findings.verification: Compared checkpoint wording with current imports and implementation status; no root documentation changed.
findings.recommendation: Refresh the checkpoint or prominently mark it historical and link the executable inventory. Distinguish arcane-category Ashglass extraction from an actual spell/ritual resource economy, and retain the original future-only labels.
